retatrutide.molecular_type: Recombinant single-chain 30-amino-acid peptide (LY3437943) with extended serum half-life through albumin binding
retatrutide.research_focus: Retatrutide is under investigation in Phase 3 trials for treatment of obesity and type 2 diabetes.
retatrutide.mechanism_summary: The peptide acts simultaneously on GIP, GLP-1, and glucagon receptors (GCGR). GIP and GLP-1 activation promotes insulin secretion and slows gastric emptying, while GCGR activation produces moderate glucagon activation that stimulates fat oxidation. This triple-agonism combination produced significantly greater weight reduction in clinical trials than single GLP-1 or GIP agonists.
retatrutide.research_context: Retatrutide (LY3437943) was developed by Eli Lilly and is currently active in Phase 3 trials (SURMOUNT-4/5, TRIUMPH). Approved in the US only within clinical trials, not as a commercial product.
retatrutide.evidence_summary: Clinical evidence: Phase 2 study (Jastreboff et al., NEJM 2023) showed dose-dependent weight reduction (up to 24.5% at 12 mg). Phase 2b/3 sub-study (Sanyal et al., Nature Medicine 2024) reduced liver fat by up to 86%. Preclinical data (Coskun et al., Cell Metabolism 2022) confirm the triple-agonist profile in animal models.
retatrutide.limitations: Long-term safety data (>48 weeks) are limited. Study populations were predominantly obese with type 2 diabetes; data on obesity alone without diabetes are limited. No long-term data in severe renal or cardiovascular disease.
